data.body_html:
June in Marbella is the sweet spot: the summer heat has arrived (28°C average), the sea has warmed to a pleasant 21°C, and the crowds haven't yet peaked. But June also brings its own weather pattern — afternoon winds that can surprise the unprepared. This guide breaks down exactly what to expect from the marbella boat rental weather june, which boats handle it best, and how to make the most of your day on the water.

June Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

June delivers 11 hours of sunshine, with UV index peaking at 8-9 — strong, so bring factor 50. Sea temperature averages 21°C, warming through the month. Air temperatures range from 22°C in the morning to 28-30°C by mid-afternoon. The main factor to plan around is wind: typically 10-14 knots from the east (Levante) in the afternoon. Mornings are calmer, making early departures ideal for smooth cruising.

How June Wind Affects Your Charter

Afternoon winds create a moderate chop, especially in open water. But don't let that put you off — our skippers know exactly how to navigate. They'll often head east towards Cabopino or west towards Estepona, where the coast offers shelter. For a smooth ride, choose a larger vessel. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) and Mangusta 80 (24m) cut through waves effortlessly. If you prefer a more intimate trip, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) is still very stable for its size.

Best Boats for June Conditions

  • For groups up to 12: Azimut 58 Flybridge — 17.6m, flybridge offers shade and wind protection.
  • For speed enthusiasts: Pershing 46 — 14m, planing hull handles chop well.
  • For luxury and space: Ferretti 94 — 29m, supreme comfort even in afternoon breeze.
  • For budget-friendly: Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 — €749/2h, ideal for a half-day trip.

All charters depart from Puerto Banús, with free parking nearby. See our full fleet and pricing for more options.

Where to Go in June: Calm Coves & Coastal Gems

With 21°C water, swimming is a must. Head to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés — sheltered coves where the water is glassy even when the wind picks up. For a longer cruise, sail towards Estepona (10 NM west) or Cabopino (8 NM east). The Marbella Marina and Puerto Banús are great for a lunch stop, with beach clubs like Ocean Club and Nikki Beach accessible by tender.

What's Included in Your June Charter

Every rental includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment and Spanish IVA (21%). So you can relax and enjoy the sun without hidden costs. For the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free for 4-hour charters — perfect for thrill-seekers.

Top Tips for a Perfect June Day

  • Book early: June is peak season — reserve at least 2 weeks ahead.
  • Start early: 10:00 AM departures get the calmest water.
  • Pack sunscreen: UV index 8-9 means reapply every 2 hours.
  • Bring a light jacket: Afternoon winds can feel cool.
  • Ask for snorkelling gear: We provide it free on request.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is June a good time to rent a boat in Marbella?

Yes, June is excellent. Air temperatures reach 28°C, sea water warms to 21°C, and you get 11 hours of sunshine. Afternoon winds pick up to 10-14 knots, but mornings are calm and perfect for cruising. It's less crowded than July and August.

What should I wear for a boat trip in June?

Bring swimwear, a light cover-up, sunglasses and high-SPF sunscreen (factor 50). Even with 28°C heat, the sea breeze can feel cool, so pack a windbreaker or light jumper. Non-slip shoes are recommended for deck safety.

Which boat is best for June winds?

Larger flybridges like the Azimut 58 or Mangusta 80 handle afternoon winds well. For a more intimate trip, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are stable and comfortable. If you want speed, the Pershing 46 cuts through chop efficiently.

Can I swim and snorkel in June?

Absolutely. Sea temperature averages 21°C, which is comfortable for swimming. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés offer sheltered coves with clear water. We provide snorkelling gear on request — just let us know when booking.

How far in advance should I book a June charter?

Book at least 2-3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends and the Azimut 58 or Mangusta 80. June is the start of peak season, and popular boats sell out quickly. For last-minute availability, contact us via WhatsApp.

What is the wind like in June on the Costa del Sol?

June typically sees a light to moderate Levante wind, 10-14 knots in the afternoon. Mornings are usually calmer. Our skippers know the best routes to minimise chop, often heading east towards Cabopino or west towards Estepona.
